question: What is the main job of the Central Sterilizing Supply Department (CSSD) in a hospital?

options.A: Processing, issuing, and controlling sterile supplies
options.B: Treating patients with severe hospital-acquired infections
options.C: Manufacturing surgical instruments for the operating theatre
options.D: Disposing of hazardous clinical waste from wards

explanation: Think of the CSSD as the hospital's central hub for all clean and sterile equipment. They make sure safe instruments are always ready for every ward and theatre! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why do hospitals use a central sterilization department instead of letting each ward clean its own instruments?

options.A: It reduces the total number of surgical instruments the hospital must buy
options.B: It allows nurses to focus solely on direct bedside patient care
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any chemical disinfectants
options.D: It guarantees consistent infection prevention standards across the facility

explanation: Having one dedicated department ensures that every single instrument goes through the exact same high-standard cleaning process, keeping patients safe everywhere. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which area in the CSSD uses negative air pressure so that dirty air or mists don't escape into other rooms?
explanation: The decontamination room is where dirty instruments are washed. Negative pressure pulls air inward, ensuring any splashes or airborne germs stay locked inside that room! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: Why must materials flow in only one direction (unidirectionally) through the CSSD?

options.A: To comply with fire safety evacuation route regulations
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination between dirty and sterile items
options.C: To speed up the physical sorting of heavy surgical trays
options.D: To ensure staff members complete their shifts on time

explanation: Items always move forward from dirty to clean! This simple rule ensures that clean, sterile equipment never crosses paths with dirty, used instruments. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which cleaning machine uses high-frequency sound waves to blast hidden dirt out of tiny instrument hinges and crevices?
explanation: Ultrasonic cleaners use tiny, rapid bubbles that collapse violently (cavitation) to scrub away dirt from places a brush could never reach! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h3)

question: What happens if dried blood or organic dirt is left on a surgical instrument before it goes into the autoclave?

options.A: It causes the metallic instruments to change color permanently
options.B: It shields trapped microbes from the sterilizing agent
options.C: It accelerates the drying cycle inside the chamber
options.D: It reacts with the steam to create a pleasant fragrance

explanation: Dirt acts like a shield! If blood or tissue dries on an instrument, the steam can't reach the germs hiding underneath, making the sterilization fail. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why do CSSD staff inspect clean instruments under a magnifying lamp before wrapping them?

options.A: To check for residual soil, cracks, or mechanical damage
options.B: To warm up the metal so it absorbs steam faster
options.C: To polish the exterior surface for aesthetic appeal
options.D: To engrave the hospital inventory number onto the metal surface

explanation: A quick look under a magnifier helps catch tiny cracks, dull edges, or leftover dirt before the instrument is packed for surgery. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the most important feature of any wrapper used for surgical instrument trays?

options.A: It must allow sterilizing agent penetration while blocking microbes
options.B: It must dissolve safely inside the autoclave chamber during the cycle
options.C: It should be completely waterproof to resist accidental liquid spills
options.D: It needs to be brightly colored for easy identification on shelves

explanation: The wrapper has a tough job: it must let the steam or gas inside to kill germs, but keep bacteria out while sitting on the shelf afterward. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the standard, go-to method for sterilizing metal instruments that can withstand heat and moisture?
explanation: The good old steam autoclave is the fastest, safest, and most reliable method for most hospital instruments! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: When would a technician choose hydrogen peroxide gas plasma instead of a standard steam autoclave?

options.A: When dealing with items that have thick layers of dried organic soil
options.B: When processing heat-sensitive and moisture-sensitive delicate equipment
options.C: When running a quick emergency cycle for general surgical scissors
options.D: When sterilizing large heavy orthopedic stainless steel container trays

explanation: Some delicate cameras or electronics would melt in a hot steam autoclave, so gas plasma is used because it runs at much lower temperatures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which type of indicator uses real, highly resistant bacterial spores to prove a sterilizer is actually killing microbes?
explanation: Biological indicators contain harmless, super-tough bacterial spores. If the machine kills them, you know it's working properly! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why are chemical indicator strips placed right inside an instrument pack before putting it in the autoclave?

options.A: To certify that the metal instruments were cleaned properly in the sink
options.B: To provide a permanent barcode label for the hospital inventory system
options.C: To confirm that the sterilizing agent successfully penetrated inside the pack
options.D: To absorb any excess moisture left over from the drying phase

explanation: Tape on the outside only shows the outside got hot. An internal strip proves the steam actually made it all the way to the center of the pack. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: What inventory rule ensures that older sterile packs are used before newer ones?
explanation: FIFO (First-In, First-Out) ensures stock doesn't sit on shelves collecting dust until it expires. Oldest items go out first! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why must transport carts carrying sterile supplies through hospital hallways be covered or enclosed?

options.A: To protect the sterile packs from environmental dust and airborne droplets
options.B: To keep unauthorized patients from stealing surgical instruments
options.C: To maintain a constant freezing temperature during transport
options.D: To prevent the heavy metal trays from sliding off the trolley

explanation: Open hallways have dust and people walking by. Enclosed carts keep sterile packs safe and clean until they reach the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: What protective gear is a must for staff washing dirty instruments in the CSSD decontamination area?

options.A: Disposable paper caps and standard cloth lab coats
options.B: Heavy lead aprons and radiation dosimeter badges
options.C: Waterproof aprons, utility gloves, and face visors
options.D: Sterile surgical gowns and sterile latex gloves

explanation: Washing involves splashes of dirty water and blood, so staff need solid fluid-resistant protection like heavy gloves, aprons, and face shields. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe infection control practice for CSSD staff?

options.A: Recapping used surgical needle tips by hand after cleaning
options.B: Placing puncture-proof sharps bins right at the point of use
options.C: Wearing heavy-duty utility gloves during manual instrument washing
options.D: Accessing emergency eye-wash stations immediately after a splash

explanation: Never recap needles by hand! It's one of the top causes of accidental needle-stick injuries in healthcare. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)
